questions.stem: Which is the correct LCS recurrence when X[i] = Y[j]?
questions.explanation: Matching characters extend the previous diagonal LCS by 1.

questions.stem: LCS runs in time:
questions.explanation: The 2D table has n*m cells, each O(1) work. SETH says no truly subquadratic improvement.

questions.stem: Why does a 1D prefix DP fail for LCS?
choices: Both inputs are simultaneously consumed; the subproblem must index both
questions.explanation: Each character of X may match different positions of Y; you cannot collapse Y to a constant. Two indices are needed.

questions.stem: In RNA secondary structure DP, the subproblem is OPT(i, j) = max pairs in substring b_i..b_j. Why is interval indexing necessary?
choices: Non-crossing pairings split the interval into two non-overlapping subintervals; the structure is recursive on intervals
questions.explanation: Pairing position t with j splits [i, j] into [i, t-1] and [t+1, j-1] — both intervals, not prefixes. Prefix DP cannot express this.

questions.stem: What is the running time of the standard RNA secondary structure DP?
questions.explanation: n^2 intervals * O(n) choices for the pairing partner = O(n^3).

questions.stem: What is the correct evaluation order for an interval DP?
questions.explanation: Smaller intervals are computed first so that the recurrence's strictly smaller subintervals are already in the table.

questions.stem: Bellman-Ford runs in time:
questions.explanation: n iterations, each relaxing all m edges. Detects negative cycles in an extra iteration.

questions.stem: What does OPT(i, v) represent in the Bellman-Ford DP from this unit?
choices: Number of edges from v to t
Min cost of v -> t path using at most i edges
Number of paths from s to v
questions.explanation: The unit's formulation computes destination-oriented values: paths to a fixed sink t using at most i edges.

questions.stem: Matrix-chain multiplication M(i, j) recurrence is:
choices: min_{k in [i, j-1]} M(i, k) + M(k+1, j) + p_{i-1} p_k p_j
questions.explanation: Split at every possible position k; cost = subchains' costs + product cost of joining them (p_{i-1} p_k p_j).

questions.stem: Matrix-chain runs in:
questions.explanation: n^2 cells (intervals), each with up to n choices: O(n^3) time, O(n^2) space.

questions.stem: Why must Bellman-Ford handle graphs with negative edges but not negative cycles?
choices: Negative cycles let shortest path go arbitrarily low
questions.explanation: A path that traverses a negative cycle repeatedly can have arbitrarily low cost; shortest-path is undefined.

questions.stem: Segmented Least Squares recurrence: OPT(j) = min over i <= j of e(i,j) + c + OPT(i-1). What does c represent?
choices: A constant cost per segment break
questions.explanation: c is the segmentation penalty added each time a new segment begins. Without it, every point would become its own segment.

questions.stem: Which problem from this week uses a 2D 'two prefixes' DP shape?
questions.explanation: LCS's subproblem is OPT(i, j) = LCS of X[1..i] with Y[1..j] — both prefix indices.

questions.stem: Which problem from this week uses an interval DP shape?
questions.explanation: RNA and matrix-chain are interval DPs; pairing splits an interval into two strictly-smaller intervals.

questions.stem: If a problem requires choosing a 'break point' anywhere inside a range, which DP shape suits it?
questions.explanation: Splitting at every internal break point is the interval-DP signature; matrix-chain and RNA are the canonical examples.

questions.stem: Space-optimised LCS that returns only the value (not the sequence) can run in:
questions.explanation: Only the current and previous row are needed; O(min(n, m)) extra space suffices when you keep the shorter dimension.

questions.stem: How many times is each e(i, j) computed in the Segmented Least Squares DP?
questions.explanation: Pre-compute each e(i, j) once into a table; the DP reuses it, keeping total cost manageable.

questions.stem: What is the base case for the LCS DP?
questions.explanation: Empty prefix has zero common subsequence length.

questions.stem: How can Bellman-Ford detect a negative cycle?
choices: Run one extra iteration; if any distance improves, a negative cycle is reachable
questions.explanation: After n-1 iterations any shortest path is final; a subsequent improvement implies a negative cycle on a reachable path.

questions.stem: Why is the RNA DP base case OPT(i, j) = 0 when j - i < 4?
choices: Biological loop-length constraint requires at least 4 unpaired bases between (i, j)
Strings of length < 4 cannot be parsed
questions.explanation: RNA pairings require a minimum loop length (commonly 4) — pairs (i, j) too close cannot exist.

questions.stem: Matrix-chain multiplication's optimal parenthesisation depends on:
questions.explanation: Multiplication cost p_{i-1} p_k p_j depends only on the dimension chain, not on entry values.

questions.stem: Bellman-Ford with push-based relaxation uses what space?
questions.explanation: Only the current distance vector needs to be stored; relax along edges in place, O(n) space.

questions.stem: Which best describes 'non-crossing' base pairs in RNA?
choices: No two pairs (i, j), (k, l) interleave (no i < k < j < l)
questions.explanation: Non-crossing is the formal constraint that lets interval DP decouple subproblems.

questions.stem: Edit distance DP between two strings of lengths n, m runs in:
questions.explanation: Edit distance has the same 2D prefix shape as LCS — O(nm) time and space.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a recognised subproblem shape from Week 5?
questions.explanation: Sparse adjacency is not a DP subproblem shape; the recognised shapes are prefixes (1D or 2D), intervals, and (item, capacity).
